{{Quote|If you get to your rivals before they're ready, you can do anything you want&mdash;including assassination.''"<br />"''It sounds like a bloodbath.''"<br />"''Normally we keep it low-key, for order's sake. Poisonings. A ''shikkar'' blade in the gut.|[[Orielle Kitai]] and [[Jelph Marrian]]|<ref name="Purgatory">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Purgatory]]''</ref>}}
'''Shikkars''' were intricate, [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-crafted [[Dagger/Legends|daggers]] made out of [[Glass/Legends|glass]] that were created and used by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] by the [[Time/Legends|time]] following the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]]. Shikkars had long, elegant blades and were prized amongst the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]] for their artistic value as well as their role as weapons. They were made for one single usage&mdash;after a shikkar was used to stab someone, the [[Hilt/Legends|hilt]] was broken off, leaving the blade embedded in the victim's body. Since the manner of [[Death/Legends|death]] suffered by shikkar was exceptionally painful, many Sith considered it an insulting form of [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]]. The weapons were crafted and employed often by members of three rival glass-crafting guilds on Kesh. [[Tura Sanga]] was famous among the Sith Tribe for crafting shikkars, and the Sith [[Seelah Korsin]] owned a shikkar that had been made by Kesh's [[Species/Legends|native]] [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]].

As the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Sorzus Syn]] noted in the ''[[Book of Sith]]'', Shikkars were frequently used by Sith for assassinations. Even [[Standard year/Legends|millennia]] after their invention, the weapons were still prominent&mdash;in [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]], several members of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith strike team|Sith strike team]] sent to [[Death/Legends|kill]] the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] carried shikkars, including [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Vestara Khai]] and her [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]], [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lady]] [[Olaris Rhea]]. Later, in [[44 ABY]], several shikkars were crafted specifically for decoration during the celebration that marked the Tribe's alliance with the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[Destructors|entity]] [[Abeloth]].

==Description==
{{Quote|The shikkar is the tool of assassins. It can be as long as a forearm, yet it is easily concealed beneath robes. A twist of the handle after stabbing a victim will snap the glassy blade off and leave it to fester beneath the skin.|Sorzus Syn's diary entry on shikkars|<ref name="BoS" />}}
[[File:Shikkar-Syn.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A shikkar illustrated by Sorzus Syn]]
Shikkars were [[Dagger/Legends|daggers]] that were crafted from [[Glass/Legends|glass]] with the application of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. They had intricate, elegant blades<ref name="Omen" /> that were up to at least ten [[Centimeter/Legends|centimeters]] in length<ref name="Abyss" />&mdash;about as long as a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Limb/Legends|forearm]]<ref name="BoS" />&mdash;and about the width of a Human finger.<ref name="Allies" /> The blades could be straight<ref name="BoS" /> or curved.<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2011 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 6|subset=Artist Sketch Cards|cardname=Shea Standefer}}</ref> The [[Hilt/Legends|hilt]] of the weapon was also designed to be long and narrow, and at least one shikkar was [[Color/Legends|colored]] black and white.<ref name="Allies" /> The weapons could easily be carried hidden beneath a being's [[Sith apparel|robes]].<ref name="BoS" /> Shikkars were valued by the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]] for their artistic virtues as much as they were for their use as weapons.<ref name="Abyss" />

The daggers were made to be used just once, and although the apparent frailty of the weapons as a whole was misleading, the point where the blade met the hilt was particularly fragile.<ref name="Allies" /> After the weapon was used to stab someone, the hilt was twisted and snapped off,<ref name="BoS" /> leaving the glass blade in the victim's body so as to cause as much pain as possible.<ref name="Abyss" /> As such, some [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] considered the use of the weapon to be particularly insulting to the target, and shikkars were frequently used as a means of getting revenge.<ref name="Apoc">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref> Also, due to the fact that shikkars were made out of nothing but glass, they could pass through [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] undetected.<ref name="Allies" />

==History==
{{Quote|I had to use his own shikkar against him, so the High Lords will assume this is a vendetta killing.|Vestara Khai, after killing Ruku Myal|<ref name="Apoc" />}}
Shikkars were invented and used by Sith for [[Assassin/Legends|assassinations]] by the [[Time/Legends|time]] following the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]], which ended around [[6900 BBY]].<ref name="Syn" /> The [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Sorzus Syn]], who lived in that era, made a diary entry that was included in the ''[[Book of Sith]]'', a [[Book/Legends|compilation]] of historical Sith writings, that mentioned the weapons.<ref name="BoS" />

In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], a group of Sith crash-landed on the remote planet Kesh after their vessel, the ''[[Omen]]'', was [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|knocked]] off-course during a [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump. The survivors were stranded there, unable to call for help or rebuild their [[Omen|ship]], and they quickly formed a new Sith Tribe.<ref name="Omen" /> Shikkars were crafted and used by members of the Tribe; [[Seelah Korsin]], [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] of the Tribe's [[Grand Lord]], [[Yaru Korsin]], owned a shikkar fashioned for her by the [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]]&mdash;the [[Species/Legends|natives]] of Kesh.<ref name="Paragon" /> By [[3960 BBY]], members of the Sith Tribe often used shikkars for advancement opportunities; Sith employed the glass daggers to subtly assassinate rivals in order to ensure their own rise within the ranks of the Tribe.<ref name="Purgatory" /> Sometime before [[3000 BBY]], [[Slippery Hilts|one]] member of the Tribe tried to assassinate another Sith with his shikkar, but he had improperly constructed his sheath, and the blade fell into his ankle. The wound became infected, and the Sith died within a month.<ref name="Secrets">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Secrets]]''</ref>

In 3000 BBY, Sith [[Caretaker]] [[Varner Hilts]] used a shikkar owned by fellow Sith [[Iliana Hilts|Iliana Merko]] to cut into the command chair in the crashed ''Omen'' to retrieve a hidden message to the Yaru Korsin from his [[Parent/Legends|mother]], [[Takara Korsin|Takara]].<ref name="Secrets" /> [[Standard year/Legends|Millennia]] later, in [[41 ABY]], shikkars were still owned by several members of the Lost Tribe,<ref name="Omen" /> who considered them to be noble weapons.<ref name="Allies" /> By that time, shikkars were commonly utilized by the members of the three Sith guilds that held an oligopoly on the profession of sculpting glass in the Kesh [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tahv]]. Those guilds crafted shikkars and other valuable objects out of glass formed from the planet's lavender sands. Members of the guilds often used their shikkars in attempts to assassinate rival guild members; to counter such attacks, the guilds began employing [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] for protection.<ref name="Omen" />

[[File:Vestaraonthehunt.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Vestara Khai, with a shikkar]]
When a [[Lost Tribe of Sith strike team|Sith strike team]] was sent to [[Death/Legends|kill]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]], several of its members carried shikkars. During the strike team's [[Skirmish at Sinkhole Station|battle]] with the Jedi at [[Sinkhole Station]], a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] in [[Maw Cluster/Legends|the Maw]], [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]] [[Yuvar Xal]] initiated a coup to take over command of the team from [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lady]] [[Olaris Rhea]]. However, Rhea's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Vestara Khai]], used her shikkar to kill Xal, throwing it into his abdomen and [[Telekinesis/Legends|using]] the Force to break off the hilt. Later, when Rhea and Khai [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|dueled]] with Skywalker, Rhea struck at the Jedi with her [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] while simultaneously using the Force to attack him with her shikkar. The blade was strong enough to rip a hole in Skywalker's [[Environment suit/Legends|combat vac suit]] before it snapped. The strike team failed to kill Skywalker, however, and Khai was the only Sith to survive the mission.<ref name="Abyss" />

Khai's father, the [[Sith Saber]] [[Gavar Khai]], owned a full personal collection of shikkars on Kesh. In [[44 ABY]], he presented one of his shikkars to Vestara in the hope that she would be able to use it to kill either Skywalker or his son, [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Ben Skywalker]]. The shikkar that he gave to her had been fashioned by the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Tura Sanga]], who was an exceptionally famous shikkar-craftsman and whose style of shikkars was decidedly unique.<ref name="Allies" /> Gavar Khai attempted to kill the elder Skywalker with a shikkar when a [[Duel at the Pool of Knowledge|duel]] broke out at the [[Pool of Knowledge]] [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]], but the attempt failed.<ref name="Vortex">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref> Later, when the dark side entity [[Abeloth]] proposed an alliance with the Sith Tribe to defeat their mutual enemy, the Jedi, she was invited to Tahv. There, several shikkars were created specifically for the celebration that was held in her honor. However, Abeloth betrayed the Sith and [[Destruction of Tahv|attacked]] the capital, destroying buildings, killing thousands of residents, and using her [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] to send shikkars flying through the city with the intent of causing harm.<ref name="Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref> The Jedi later embarked on a mission to defeat the Sith on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] capital planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]; during the mission, Vestara Khai stabbed Sith Master [[Ruku Myal]] with his own shikkar.<ref name="Apoc" />

==Behind the scenes==
Shikkars were first introduced in author [[Christie Golden]]'s ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]'', the second novel in the nine-part [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series. The glass weapons subsequently appeared in the third, fifth, sixth, eighth, and ninth novels of the series, titled ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss]]'', ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]'', ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]'', ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]'', and ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]'', respectively. Shikkars also appeared in ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''&mdash;the third installment in the ongoing [[Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith|''Lost Tribe of the Sith'']] [[eBook]] series, which serves as a tie-in to the ''Fate of the Jedi'' saga&mdash;and later received mention in the fourth, fifth, sixth, and eighth entries in the series, respectively titled [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior|''Savior'']], [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Purgatory|''Purgatory'']], [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Sentinel|''Sentinel'']], and [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Secrets|''Secrets'']]. Shikkars were also mentioned in Golden's short story, "[[First Blood (short story)|First Blood]]."

A shikkar was pictured in the [[Topps|The Topps Company, Inc.'s]] ''[[2011 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 6]]'' cards sketched by [[Shea Standefer]]. Shikkars were later mentioned in the ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'' reference book by [[Daniel Wallace]], which was published as an [[in-universe]] compilation of Sith writings.
